summary.title: Keras vs. TensorFlow - Which one is better and which one should I learn?
summary.one_liner: Learn why the Keras vs. TensorFlow choice is a false one, since tf.keras is built into TensorFlow, and see MiniVGGNet trained on CIFAR-10 both ways, including a custom CRELU activation.
keywords: which deep learning library to learn
keras or tensorflow which is better
takeaways: Since mid-2017 Keras is integrated into TensorFlow as tf.keras, so you can use the Keras API and drop into raw TensorFlow code when needed.
Standalone Keras still works independently of TensorFlow; the author recommends using tf.keras if you work in TensorFlow.
The same MiniVGGNet CNN can be written with standard keras or tf.keras with nearly identical code.
A custom TensorFlow function (CRELU via a Lambda layer) can be inserted directly into a Keras model.
On the author's CPU, training for 30 epochs on CIFAR-10 reached about 75% test accuracy, with each epoch taking a little over 5 minutes.
summary.summary: The author argues that asking whether to use Keras or TensorFlow is the wrong question, because Keras has been integrated into TensorFlow as tf.keras. He shows a small feedforward network written in both styles, then builds a MiniVGGNet CNN twice, once with standalone Keras and once with tf.keras. The tf.keras version swaps one activation for a custom CRELU implemented with a TensorFlow function in a Lambda layer. Both scripts train on CIFAR-10 for 30 epochs with SGD, and the Keras run reports about 75% test accuracy. The page is a code-walkthrough tutorial with the full downloads linked from the post.
